In [[geometry]], a '''rectified 120-cell''' is a [[uniform 4-polytope]] formed as the [[Rectification (geometry)|rectification]] of the regular [[120-cell]].

[[Emanuel Lodewijk Elte|E. L. Elte]] identified it in 1912 as a semiregular polytope, labeling it as tC<sub>120</sub>.

There are four rectifications of the 120-cell, including the zeroth, the 120-cell itself. The birectified 120-cell is more easily seen as a rectified 600-cell, and the trirectified 120-cell is the same as the dual 600-cell.

[[File:Rectified hecatonicosachoron net.png|thumb|right|[[Net (polyhedron)|Net]]]]
In [[geometry]], the '''[[Rectification (geometry)|rectified]] [[120-cell]]''' or '''rectified hecatonicosachoron''' is a convex [[uniform 4-polytope]] composed of 600 regular [[tetrahedron|tetrahedra]] and 120 [[icosidodecahedron|icosidodecahedra]] [[cell (mathematics)|cells]]. Its vertex figure is a [[triangular prism]], with three icosidodecahedra and two tetrahedra meeting at each vertex.

Alternative names:
* Rectified 120-cell ([[Norman Johnson (mathematician)|Norman Johnson]])
* Rectified hecatonicosichoron / rectified dodecacontachoron / rectified polydodecahedron
* Icosidodecahedral hexacosihecatonicosachoron
* Rahi (Jonathan Bowers: for rectified hecatonicosachoron)
* Ambohecatonicosachoron ([[John Horton Conway|Neil Sloane & John Horton Conway]])
